CVE-2026-116243.title: pgAdmin 4: Utility binary path can point at a shared storage directory
CVE-2026-116243.description:
pgAdmin 4 runs pg_dump, pg_restore, pg_dumpall and psql from the binary path a user sets in their preferences. In server mode the binary path was refused only when it lay under the per-user storage directory (STORAGE_DIR), not under a SHARED_STORAGE directory, which ordinary users can upload files to. A user could therefore upload an executable to shared storage, point their binary path at it, and have pgAdmin run it as the operating-system account running pgAdmin. On POSIX, files created through pgAdmin are not executable, so this is exploitable where any file with an executable name can run, such as Windows server mode.

The fix checks the binary path against every SHARED_STORAGE directory as well, after expanding $DIR, collapsing ".." and resolving symbolic links, compares directories in a way a different spelling on a case-insensitive filesystem cannot bypass, refuses a path containing a NUL, and enforces the check wherever binary paths are resolved, including for the PSQL…

CVE-2026-128075.description: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. CVE-2026-133839.title: FlowIntel Missing Authorization Check Allows Unauthorized Deletion of Evidence Files from Restricted Privileged Tasks
CVE-2026-133839.description:
FlowIntel contains a missing authorization vulnerability in its task file deletion functionality. When a privileged task is in a restricted state (Requested, Rejected, or Request Review), any authenticated user with basic case membership (e.g., editor or queuer) was able to delete evidence files associated with that task via both the browser interface and the REST API. The deletion operation should have been restricted to users holding Admin, Case Admin, or Queue Admin roles.

The vulnerability affects the core file deletion logic, the browser-facing task endpoint, and the API task endpoint. No role-based restriction was enforced prior to performing disk removal, database record deletion, timeline event removal, or history log updates.

An attacker with a low-privilege case membership could destroy evidence files, corrupt investigation timelines, and alter case history, compromising the integrity of ongoing investigations.

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0.

CVE-2026-63505.title: Probo: Cross-tenant IDOR via unvalidated FK references
CVE-2026-63505.description: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.223.1, Probo's console GraphQL API is a multi-tenant GRC platform where all data is scoped to an organization. A Finding can reference a Risk via finding.riskId. That reference is stored without validating that the risk belongs to the caller's organization, and the Finding.risk field resolver authorizes the finding (caller's org) instead of the risk, then loads the risk with a tenant scope derived from the risk's own global ID. The stored cross-tenant reference also blocks B from deleting its own risk (ON DELETE RESTRICT), a cross-tenant integrity/DoS. This issue has been patched in version 0.223.1.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: validate transport name in listener_set before serv creation

nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() holds nfsd_mutex for the whole listener
teardown and rebuild. The code checks NFSD_A_SOCK_TRANSPORT_NAME for
presence only, and not for content. An arbitrary name therefore reaches
svc_xprt_create_from_sa(). There, a name that matches no registered class
calls request_module("svc%s", name). That call is a TASK_KILLABLE usermode
helper upcall, and it runs under nfsd_mutex.

Check the name against the classes that NFSD can create: tcp, udp and
rdma. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), which runs before
the code takes nfsd_mutex. The rejection names the offending attribute
through extack, since -EPROTONOSUPPORT on its own does not say which
entry carried the bad name.

This narrows the upcall. It does not remove it. NFSD accepts "rdma"
without a condition, so on a kernel that does not build svcrdma the name
still…
